$comment: #NEW-136: THE MODEL FALLBACK of the issue search (slice 5 of #NEW-131), its pure half: when the row shows, the ONE prompt, and the sanitizer that turns a model's answer into a query. DECISIONS (Danny, 2026-11-24): (1) EXPLICIT, never automatic: typing never calls a model. In the GLOBAL issue search, when the phrase grammar (issue-search-phrase.json) answers null for the typed text AND wants(text) holds, the list's top row is the SAME Picker action row as the `Search: <query>` suggestion (search-list.json SUGGESTION, `suggestion.translate`), named `Translate to a search`: same icon by concept, same position, never both rows at once. Picking it runs the model; while it runs the row carries the existing spinner in its trailing slot (no new component, no subtitle) and a second pick does nothing. Success: the field's text is replaced by the query, the focus stays, the search re-runs. Failure, a timeout or an answer the sanitizer rejects: the toast `Couldn't translate this search` (feedback-states.json: a failed action = toast), the field stays as typed and the row is offered again. (2) WHERE: the desktop app (every OS) and iOS 26+ with Apple Intelligence available. Web and Android show NO row (no local model; Android has no caller, so there is no Kotlin port). (3) DESKTOP MODEL: the signed-in claude CLI of the user's own login (the profile a launch would run on), model `limits.model`, ONE print-mode call: the prompt on stdin, `system` as the system prompt, no tools, no MCP servers, no settings, no session row, no transcript, nothing shown in chats, killed after `limits.timeoutSeconds` and when the sheet closes or the text changes. No signed-in claude login = no row. Never a hosted agent, never our server, never resold tokens; the macOS desktop app uses this path too. (4) iOS MODEL: Apple Foundation Models on the device (`#available(iOS 26, *)`, `SystemLanguageModel.default.availability == .available`), `system` as the session's instructions. Older iOS, an unsupported device, Apple Intelligence off or the model not ready = no row. WANTS (`wantsCases`: {name, now, members, text, expected}): true when the trimmed text is at most `limits.maxTextLength` code points, has `limits.minWords` or more WORDS (whitespace-separated tokens that, stripped of leading and trailing . , ; : ! ? " ' ( ), hold a letter or digit), no token starts with by: is: status: created: updated: or similar: (lowercased, stripped the same way), and the phrase grammar answers null. SANITIZE (`sanitizeCases`: {name, now, members, text, output, expected: string | null}); the model's output is NEVER trusted. LINE: the first line of the output that is non-empty after cleaning; cleaning = trim, a line that starts with a code fence (three backticks) and does not also end with a backtick is dropped, then leading and trailing whitespace and wrap characters (backtick, " ' * and the typographic quotes) go, then ONE leading `search:` or `query:` (any case) with the wrap characters after it. TOKENS: the engine's (issue-search.json: trimmed, one leading # dropped, lowercased, split on whitespace), the first `limits.maxTokens` of them. Each token: `is:open|closed` stays, any other is: goes; `status:<v>` stays when v is ONE word of letters and digits at most `limits.maxWordLength` long, else goes; `by:<v>` (one leading @ dropped) stays ONLY when v is a name word or the email local part of a member (the grammar's member rule), else v becomes a plain word; `created:<v>` / `updated:<v>` stay when the engine parses v as a range (`parseIssueSearchRange`), else go; EVERY other token holding a colon goes (similar:, a URL, a made-up filter); the rest are plain words: stripped of the punctuation above, kept when they hold a letter or digit and are at most `limits.maxWordLength` code points, the first `limits.maxWords` different ones. RESULT: is: tokens, status: tokens, by: tokens, the dates, then the words, each in first-seen order without repeats, joined by one space; null when nothing is left, null when it equals the text's own engine tokens joined (nothing changed). PROMPT (`promptCases`: {name, now, members, text, expected}): ONE string, byte for byte the same on desktop and iOS: the token syntax, the members' FIRST names only (the first name word of each, lowercased, no repeats, at most `limits.maxNames`; never an email, a member without a name is left out, and without any name the by: line and its example are left out), today's UTC date, `Answer with one line, the query only.`, German and English examples, then `Sentence: ` and the text (whitespace collapsed, its first `limits.maxTextLength` code points). `system` is the instruction line beside it. REPLAYED: web `apps/web/src/lib/issue-search-translation.ts` (the reference; web never calls a model), desktop `domain::issue_search_translation`, iOS ExpCore `IssueSearchTranslation`; same case names.
